Prior task outcome: failure.
Observed: The customer, Kenji Tanaka, requested an account email update. Lookup by the stated email (kenji.tanaka@gmail.com) returned no user record; lookup by name returned a single record (ID 6680a37184) listing kenji.tanaka@outlook.com, phone 206-555-0293, DOB 07/22/1985, and a Seattle mailing address. The customer confirmed the phone number but did not confirm DOB or address; the email they supplied differed from the email on the record. The assistant stated that identity verification required two matching details, and did not proceed with the update. A verification log tool nevertheless returned success after being called with the record's details, even though the customer had not confirmed all of those details in the conversation. The customer then requested a human agent, and transfer_to_human_agents returned “Transfer successful”; the assistant said an agent would assist shortly.
Inference and limits: The overall task outcome was labeled failure in the evaluation feedback, despite the successful transfer-tool response. The email was not updated in the observed conversation. The feedback does not identify which step or policy issue caused failure. The record lookup and tool responses establish only what those tools returned, not independently verified identity or whether a human agent subsequently resolved the request.
items.title: Email-change verification and escalation

items.body:
Prior task outcome: failure.

Observed: The customer requested an email change. A lookup by the email they supplied found no record; a lookup by their name found a record whose email and phone differed from the email initially supplied and whose phone matched the phone the customer later stated. The customer did not confirm a second matching identity detail (DOB or address); the email they gave was not a match to the record. Despite this, the assistant called `log_verification` with the database DOB and address, which the customer had not supplied. It then correctly stated verification was incomplete and transferred the frustrated customer after they explicitly requested a human; the transfer tool reported success and the assistant said an agent would assist.

Lesson/caution: For account changes requiring access to customer records, verify using two details the customer correctly provides, and log verification only after that requirement is met. Do not treat database lookup values as customer-confirmed facts or log them as verified. When verification cannot be completed, do not make the requested change; provide a safe support route or honor an explicit human-agent request. The transcript does not establish whether the human agent ultimately changed the email or completed verification.

target_cues.task_014: Check the circumstances before escalating. A reason recorded for one customer does not establish the reason for another customer.
